takeaways: Refiners are having a moment. Marathon earned $26.93 a share adjusted, almost 9x the $3.01 from a year ago, and beat the $25.38 estimate.

The driver is refining margins: $45.70 a barrel vs $17.60 a year ago, with crude utilization at 100% (company release via TradingKey/Reuters). With oil near $97, the spread between crude and fuel is enormous.
It returned $3.3 billion to shareholders and raised the quarterly dividend 10%. MPLX, its pipeline partner, raised its payout 12.5%.
It plans to divest its Mid-Con assets, including two refineries to CVR Energy per Reuters, and reinvest mainly on the Gulf Coast.
No numeric guidance for next quarter in the release, so we leave that out.
verdict: When the world is short on gasoline, the people who make gasoline get very rich, very fast. Nine times last year's earnings is not a typo. The catch: margins this fat rarely stay this fat, and the market prices refiners like everyone knows it.

sources.title: Reuters via StreetInsider: Marathon to sell two refineries to CVR
